about: The binary surface a plugin built for Horos or OsiriX (.horosplugin, .osirixplugin) looks up in the application without being rebuilt; tests/test-legacy-plugin-abi.py checks it against the built bundle. That surface is contract, and nothing leaves this registry. Sources of the declarations: the headers of the SDK of Horos v4.0.0 RC5 (project version 20220801, with the first changes of this fork), the code this application started from, which are the headers at the top of Horos/Sources, Nitrogen/Sources and Nitrogen/Sources/JSON, the headers DCM.framework built as public, and of cocoahttpserver those of the classes the SDK's classes extend or name (AsyncSocket.h, HTTPServer.h, HTTPConnection.h, HTTPResponse.h, DDKeychain.h), kdu_OsiriXSupport.h of Horos/Sources among them, which declares the four Kakadu functions; the headers of the Horos.framework SDK of IsiX 5.3.4, rebuilt with that version's own API-Headers.pl and publish-swift-header.py, together with the headers and the generated Horos-Swift.h of its last Release package (arm64); the copies of the OsiriX SDK inside horosproject/horosplugins (revision 6b4036242ca4) for the names only they declare (the vector functions named for another processor, the notification of a plugin download); and the host methods the plugins of horosplugins call without an SDK declaring them (used_outside_sdk). An item is recorded when one SDK had both its declaration and its definition: what the headers of Horos declare, when a source that the project of Horos compiled defined it; what any of these headers declare, when IsiX 5.4.0 (build 2026110400, arm64), which loaded these plugins, exported or implemented it, or the current build does. classes: by their Objective-C runtime name, with the superclass Horos gave them, or the one they had in 5.3.4 when Horos did not have the class; a superclass recorded before stays when it leads to the one of Horos (SRView and ROIVolumeView under HorosSceneView, itself under VTKView). Four keep the superclass they have today, which is the decided exception, because the one Horos gave them is a class of the system or of a library that the application no longer descends from: DCMView and NavigatorView (NSOpenGLView then, NSView now), DCMCalendarDate (NSCalendarDate, NSDate) and VTKView (vtkCocoaGLView, NSView). selectors: 'Class -selector' or 'Class +selector', including the accessors Core Data generates for the entities of the application's models. ivars: 'Class.ivar', checked through the _OBJC_IVAR_$_Class.ivar symbol; those Horos declared @private or @package were never exported and are not listed. symbols: the exported constants, notification names, globals a plugin can write and C functions, whatever their type; a function with C++ linkage keeps its mangled name, as the C++ functions and operators of N2Operators.h and N2MinMax.h do. frameworks: the SDK frameworks a plugin's load commands name, with the symbols they exported. "sdk_selectors" lists every selector the headers of Horos declared and its sources implemented, with the header and the line of its declaration: each is also in "selectors" and comes back as a facade when a reorganization takes it out; one may be listed as missing only while its class, or the class of an object it takes, is missing. "isix5_additions" lists the classes and symbols that the headers of IsiX 5.3.4 declare and no source of Horos defined, each with the header that declares it: Horos never had them, so no plugin built for Horos or OsiriX looks them up, and they alone, of the classes and symbols, may be listed as missing, with the reason "added by the IsiX 5 SDK: Horos did not define it". Every other class, symbol and framework is there or the test fails: the few that Horos compiled without declaring them, which the IsiX 5 SDK then declared, are no additions, and the four of them that had left the application (the classes DCMTKStoreSCUOperation and HorosROIStatistics, the functions PFMoveToApplicationsFolderIfNecessary and sortPluginArrayByName) are back as facades. missing: what the application lacks today, each with its reason; it only shrinks. A selector or an instance variable that a known plugin uses may not be listed, whatever the reason. Left out: 127 C functions the header defines static or inline; 1 C++ functions of the baseline whose mangled name no build has; 73 classes no build exported and the baseline did not compile; 14 classes the baseline compiled and kept out of its headers, which the later SDK declared and no build of it exported; 467 instance variables no build exported; 68 instance variables that were @private or @package; 14 names only declared, which neither a build nor the baseline defined; 272 properties the baseline declared @dynamic, which the runtime answers; 657 selectors no class implemented. In that sentence the baseline is that Horos and the later SDK the one of IsiX 5.3.4. Also left out: protocols, since a plugin carries its own copy of every protocol it uses; the globals Horos exported that no header of an SDK declares; and what a header declares for PowerPC alone. The value of a selector, ivar or symbol is the number of horosplugins plugins whose sources reference it, as tools/inventory-plugin-api.py attributes it against the headers of both SDKs (static and textual; 0 for none). The classes of the SDK that had left the application are back with the superclass the SDK gave them; N2SingletonObject is listed with the instance variable its subclasses read, and AsyncSocketException and AsyncSocketErrorDomain with the symbols. A class that came back as a facade keeps its state in Swift stored properties: its instance variables stay in missing, with that reason, until they are exported. The instance variables of a class implemented in Swift are exported from stored fields of the class, each through a linker alias of its field's offset: Horos/Scripts/Horos/legacy-plugin-ivars.json is the table of those fields, with the type the SDK declared, the state and the ownership of each, and every entry of it is in ivars and none in missing. One that is still in missing waits for its storage to be a field of the class with the SDK's type, and says so. Added to ivars with that table, declared by the headers of the SDK and exported by the application though the 5.3.4 executable no longer exported them: DCMView.fontListGL, DCMView.labelFontListGL, DCMView.pTextureName, DCMView.blendingTextureName, DCMView.stringTextureCache, DCMView.lensTexture, DCMView.loupeTextureID, DCMView.loupeTextureWidth, DCMView.loupeTextureHeight, DCMView.loupeTextureBuffer, DCMView.loupeMaskTextureID, DCMView.loupeMaskTextureWidth, DCMView.loupeMaskTextureHeight, DCMView.loupeMaskTextureBuffer, AppController.filtersMenu, AppController.roisMenu, N2ManagedDatabase._managedObjectContext, N2ManagedDatabase._mainDatabase, N2ManagedDatabase._isDeallocating, N2ManagedDatabase.associatedThread. Those thirty-nine are declared, each with the type its field has here, by the copies of DCMView.h in the folders OsiriX Headers of the plugins of horosproject/horosplugins (revision 6b4036242ca4), none of which has them all, and DCMView.warningNotice by the copy in VoxelVolume/OsiriXAPI.framework of the same revision alone. osirix_selectors names the selectors that only the headers the OsiriX SDK publishes as text for plugin developers declare, or that the type those headers give an object asks of it, each with the header it comes from; every one of them is in selectors too, and is contract as the rest.

host_resolution.1 executable: The application's executable defined every class, method, instance variable, constant and C function of the SDK; the SDK frameworks carried none of them. A plugin reached them through the symbols the executable exported and the Objective-C metadata the runtime registered from it.
host_resolution.2 export options: Application target, Debug and Release: no EXPORTED_SYMBOLS_FILE and no -exported_symbols_list, OTHER_CFLAGS -fvisibility=default and GCC_SYMBOLS_PRIVATE_EXTERN = NO, so every global symbol was exported; Release also set KEEP_PRIVATE_EXTERNS = YES. No STRIP_STYLE was set and a build that is not installed is not stripped. DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING = YES in both configurations dropped C functions and constants nothing in the application referenced, unless marked __attribute__((used)), as the string constants of the plugin headers were. Instance variables declared @private or @package were private externs, never exported.
host_resolution.3 plugin linking: 78 of the 81 plugin projects of horosplugins link with -undefined dynamic_lookup: their references to host symbols are flat lookups that dyld resolves in any loaded image, the executable and the frameworks it loads. A plugin linked with BUNDLE_LOADER binds them to the main executable. Either way the symbol must be exported by the executable or by a framework in the bundle, and a selector is found at run time in the class's method lists.
host_resolution.4 frameworks: The API target built Horos.framework, install name @executable_path/../Frameworks/Horos.framework/Versions/A/Horos, from HorosAPI.m, which only defines the HorosAPI, OsiriXAPI, OsiriX_Headers and HorosDCM version numbers and strings, with the SDK headers. The application linked it and copied it into Contents/Frameworks; API.sh copied it again as HorosAPI, OsiriXAPI, 'OsiriX Headers' and HorosDCM (binary renamed, headers dropped, bundle identifier rewritten, install name left as Horos.framework's), because plugins were hard-linked against those names over the years. The App Store channel removed the four copies. A plugin whose load command names one of them does not load when the file is missing.
host_resolution.5 DCM.framework: DCM.framework, which the application linked and embedded, defined the DCM classes (DCMObject, DCMAttributeTag, DCMTransferSyntax and the others) and DCM functions; their headers were in the SDK and a plugin found them by flat lookup in that image. No plugin of horosplugins names DCM.framework in a load command. DCM.framework is gone; its classes are the Swift dataset model of the application now, under the same Objective-C names, found by the same flat lookup in the executable.
host_resolution.6 headers: The SDK published every .h of Horos/Sources (except the +SwiftIvars.h accessors and ROICanvasGL.h), of Nitrogen/Sources and Nitrogen/Sources/JSON, cocoahttpserver's DDKeychain.h, the generated Horos-Swift.h, and the headers the application's bridging header reaches (the DCM framework, cocoahttpserver, preference panes and helpers).
host_resolution.7 static zlib: The executable also carried the copy of zlib 1.2.3 inside GDCM (GDCM/Utilities/gdcmzlib): GDCM was built without GDCM_USE_SYSTEM_ZLIB, so that copy was linked statically, under the library's own names, which it prefixes only under Z_PREFIX, and its globals were exported like every other. A plugin linked with BUNDLE_LOADER, which did not need to name the system's zlib, had its zlib references bound to the executable. Dead-code stripping kept the functions the application reached, a set no source gives: symbols has every function that copy's zlib.h declares ZEXTERN, 58 of them, and the executable defines each one, as a call into the system's zlib.
